title: Offline Cost Estimator SDK & Simulation Playground PRD
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This PRD defines the requirements for an Offline Cost Estimator SDK and an accompanying Simulation Playground (local + hosted) that lets developers and platform teams accurately estimate Redwood Inference cost and latency for candidate prompts, model variants, sequence lengths, and batching strategies before committing to hosted or Dedicated capacity. The goal is to reduce customer time-to-confidence when evaluating price/performance trade-offs, reduce support load for cost-related questions, and increase conversion from trial-to-paid by removing cost uncertainty.

Context and problem statement:

- Customers frequently request examples that show "realistic" cost for their workload (token distribution, concurrency, latency constraints).
- Current pricing guidance in the Console is high-level and often requires manual tests against hosted endpoints; this is slow, noisy, and expensive for customers on a budget.
- Platform teams need a reproducible way to reason about how choices (quantization, batch size, prefix caching) affect per-token cost and tail latency.

Objectives (measurable):

1. Provide an SDK that can run an offline simulation that estimates per-request token cost and expected latency percentile for a given workload profile with >= 85% correlation to production measurements across supported model variants (baseline measured against hosted API).
2. Ship a web-based Simulation Playground that accepts prompt samples, model selection, batch/concurrency settings, and returns an itemized cost/lantency report within 10s for typical inputs (<= 10 prompts).
3. Reduce average pre-sale engineering time answering cost questions by 40% within 6 months of launch.
4. Achieve 20% higher conversion for trials that use the playground vs those that do not (measured in A/B pilot).

Non-goals:

- The simulator will not run full model inference locally (no model weights required).
- Not intended to replace full production performance benchmarking runs on Dedicated.

User personas:

- Developer evaluating whether Redwood fits budget and latency needs for an LLM feature.
- Platform engineer sizing Dedicated capacity for product teams.
- Solutions engineer preparing a customer TCO estimate.

High-level product components:

- Cost Estimator SDK (Python + Node.js): offline library that ingests prompt traces or synthetic workload profiles and outputs cost/latency estimates, per-token breakdown, and recommended serving configuration.
- Simulation Playground (Hosted + Local dev mode): interactive web UI that wraps the SDK, provides visualizations, and stores simulation snapshots in customer account (hosted mode).
- Server-side microservice (hosted): lightweight service that runs stochastic models and keeps up-to-date kernel/throughput profiles for each model variant.
- Reference datasets and sample prompts: small corpus of workload templates for common verticals (search, summarization, chat, extraction).

Functional requirements (numbered):

1) SDK: simple programmatic interface
   1.1 install: pip install redwood-estimator or npm i @redwood/estimator
   1.2 API: estimate = Estimator.simulate(profile, options) -> returns JSON report with fields: estimated_cost_usd, token_breakdown, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, assumptions_list
   1.3 Profile inputs: list of prompts OR workload distribution file (json lines with {prompt, tokens, frequency}).
   1.4 Options: model_variant, quantization_profile, batch_size_range, concurrency, prefix_cache_hit_rate, region_hint.
   1.5 Output: machine-readable report + human summary string.

2) Simulation accuracy model
   2.1 Maintain a release-managed set of throughput / kernel profiles for each model_variant & hardware class (A100, L40s, T4-equivalent).
   2.2 Simulation uses a queuing model that incorporates batching delays, KV cache hit-rate, and tail-latency amplification under concurrency.
   2.3 Default accuracy target: median error <= 15% for p50 latency and <= 25% for p95 vs hosted baseline for standard workloads.

3) Playground UI
   3.1 UI accepts pasted prompts, sample sets, or file uploads (jsonl).
   3.2 Runs a simulation via hosted microservice or local SDK (user choice).
   3.3 Visualizes: token histogram, per-token cost bar, latency percentiles, sensitivity matrix for batch size vs cost/latency.
   3.4 Exportable PDF/CSV TCO report with assumptions and recommended deployment configuration.

4) Security and privacy
   4.1 All hosted playground simulations must be optioned to scrub PII by default.
   4.2 For hosted mode, customer data retention for simulation artifacts is 30 days unless the customer opts in for longer retention (admin setting).
   4.3 Local dev mode must be clearly labeled to prevent accidental uploads to hosted service.

5) Telemetry and metrics
   5.1 Track usage funnels: SDK install -> run -> export; Playground open -> run -> export.
   5.2 Measure correlation telemetry: customers may opt-in to send anonymized sample traces for model calibration; store mapping to simulation snapshots.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics:

- SDK unit tests and integration tests cover simulation logic and edge cases (100% of critical code paths).
- A/B pilot across 50 trial accounts shows at least 10% reduction in average time to first paid commit for those using simulator within 3 months of pilot.
- Simulation median error <= 15% on internal validation corpus across supported models.

Placeholders for configuration table (example):

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| model_variant | string | rwd-7b-v1 | One of documented variants |
| hardware_class | enum | a100 | a100 | l40s | t4 |
| batch_size | int or [min,max] | 8 | Batch sizes tested in range |
| concurrency | int | 4 | concurrent requests per worker |
| prefix_cache_hit_rate | float | 0.3 | 0.0 - 1.0 |
| quant_profile | string | q8_0 | quantization profile to approximate token throughput |

Example SDK usage (Python):
from redwood_estimator import Estimator
profile = {"prompts": ["Summarize this document in 50 words."], "tokens_per_prompt": [120], "frequency": [1]}
est = Estimator.load_latest_profiles()
report = est.simulate(profile, options={"model_variant":"rwd-13b-v1","batch_size":8,"concurrency":2})
print(report["human_summary"])

UX flow (Playground):

1. User selects mode: local / hosted
2. Uploads or pastes prompts; optionally selects sample workload templates
3. Chooses model variant + quantization hint + hardware class
4. Runs simulation -> receives itemized report and visualization
5. Optionally exports PDF/CSV and saves snapshot to account (hosted).

Rollout plan and phases:

- Phase 0 (MVP - 6 weeks): Python SDK + hosted microservice with baseline profiles for 3 model variants and 2 hardware classes; web Playground UI with basic visualization; internal pilot with Solutions/SE.
- Phase 1 (8 weeks): Node SDK, more model/hardware coverage, exportable reports, retention controls, opt-in telemetry for calibration.
- Phase 2 (quarterly): Integration into Console account onboarding; experiment A/B for trial conversion; add recommendations engine to propose Dedicated commitments.

Security, compliance, and privacy considerations:

- Hosted microservice must be SOC2-ready: logging, access control, and encryption in transit + at rest for simulation snapshots.
- PII scrubbing defaults and explicit data deletion endpoints for simulation artifacts.
- For private deployments (Private customers), provide an on-prem simulator package that uses the same profiles but operates entirely in-customer network (packaging requirements in eng-private-deployments).

Dependencies and open questions:

- Dependency on eng-serving-runtime to provide and publish kernel/throughput profiles per model variant.
- Decision: how frequently to refresh throughput profiles (weekly vs monthly) — affects accuracy and complexity.
- Pricing implication: do we charge for hosted simulation runs beyond a free tier? Need Finance/Go-to-market input.

Pricing and packaging notes (initial guidance):

- Free tier: 10 hosted simulation runs per account per month for trials; exports disabled after free tier.
- Starter: 500 runs / month in hosted playground bundle included in developer credits for Standard customers.
- Enterprise: Simulation snapshot retention and bulk export capability included in Dedicated/Private contracts as an add-on.

QA and release checklist (minimum):

1. SDK linting, unit tests, and CI pipeline integration.
2. Simulation cross-check job against hosted API for 1000 sample traces (regression < target thresholds).
3. Security review and PII-scrubbing verification.
4. Docs: SDK README, Playground user guide, API reference, and sales one-pager.
5. Pilot with Solutions/SE for at least 10 customers before general availability.

Owner and operational contact:

Appendix: calibration experiment (short):

1) Collect 200 representative traces across search, chat, and summarization verticals using hosted API (anonymized).
2) Run offline simulations with current profiles, compute error distribution for p50/p95 latency and per-token cost.
3) Tune the queuing model parameters (batch formation latency, inter-arrival distribution) to minimize median error.
